title: Kernels and cokernels of derived complete modules for a regular principal parameter
statement:
Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-étale site in the fixed universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site and let $t\in\Gamma(T,R)$ be a global section such that multiplication $t:R\to R$ is a monomorphism of module sheaves. Write $Q_n=R/t^nR$ for the sheaf quotient ring, for $n\geq1$, and use the ordinary unbounded category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor is the total sheaf tensor evaluated on a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets the $Q_n$-action along $R\to Q_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The quotient transitions $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ specify the strict derived reduction tower. Let $C_t(K)=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_RQ_n)$, with total right-derived inverse limit, and let $c_K:K\to C_t(K)$ be its canonical map induced by the quotient projections; use strict tower resolutions, hence the augmented Roos model of the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit]. Call an $R$-module $N$ complete here when $c_{N[0]}$ is an isomorphism.

For every morphism $g:M\to N$ of complete $R$-module sheaves, $\ker g$, $\operatorname{coker}g$, and $\operatorname{im}g$ are complete. If $0\to M\to P\to N\to0$ is a short exact sequence and $M,N$ are complete, then $P$ is complete. All kernels, cokernels and images are those in the abelian category of module sheaves. No finite presentation, constructibility, or classical separatedness assumption on these modules is imposed; there is no assertion that an arbitrary submodule of a complete module is complete.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.14, printed p.23; Definition 3.4.1 and Lemma 3.4.12 identify completeness with the principal Koszul limit when t is regular; Propositions 3.1.9 and 4.2.8 supply exact countable products on a pro-etale topos. This is the regular-principal quotient-tower formulation, not a claim of closure under arbitrary subobjects.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-principal-complete-product-criterion] to identify completeness of each module with invertibility of its explicit countable scalar difference.

The product-of-epimorphisms hypothesis of [lem-sfb-countable-scalar-difference-closure] follows by taking constant families in [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Apply that closure result and transport each of its kernel, cokernel, image and extension conclusions through the criterion.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 3.1.11 and Lemmas 3.4.12, 3.4.14; the two-term Roos computation is combined with exact functor comparisons instead of the cone-amplitude argument.

split_report.summary: Followed Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 3.4.14 using the repeated-scalar inverse-limit functor. Added one computational fiber-triangle node for the specified regular-principal quotient completion unit, reused the existing exact-product and strict Roos cone/shift calculus, and wrote the cone truncation and disjoint-amplitude argument explicitly. Statement unchanged; kernel/cokernel closure is proved for maps between complete modules, then image and extension closure follow. No arbitrary-subobject claim is made.
split_report.blueprint: Serves the supported scalar-heart completeness input descending from det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle, Refinement isomorphisms paragraph, via det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement (2), first paragraph (direct-sum preservation). The latest blueprint has no statement of this general regular-principal computational lemma.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact countable products of modules over any ring sheaf on a scheme pro-etale site; needed for the scalar Roos two-term bound.
Generic strict Roos functor for arbitrary ring-sheaf complexes supplies its quasi-isomorphism, cone and shift comparisons; no compactification argument is replaced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N7-8a7ee8d4d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and all cited statements in full, and checked the item's 7 steps against Bhatt–Scholze arXiv 1309.1198: Def 3.4.1 and Lemmas 3.4.9, 3.4.12 and 3.4.14 (pp.20–23). The statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1: the Roos functor of lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus is applied to the tower (K,t) for an arbitrary ring sheaf R. Its qis, cone and shift comparisons make T_t exact. For a module the representative sits in degrees 0,1. Step 2: the LES makes c_K invertible iff T_t(K)=0, and I checked both directions. Steps 3–5 are BS 3.4.14. The triangle A[1]→[M→N]→B[0]→A[2] comes from the cone/SES Mathlib leaf. Shifting gives H^q T(B)=H^{q+2} T(A), with supports {0,1} and {−2,−1}, so both vanish. Step 6 gets im g as coker(ker g→M). Step 7 is the extension LES. New node lem-sfb-regular-principal-completion-fiber: I proved it myself. For K-flat P, regular t makes Cone(t^n) qis to P⊗Q_n with transitions (x,ty). That tower is Cone of f:(P,t)→(P,id) with f_n=t^n. H(P,id)≃P with inverse ev_1, so the first arrow is ev_1∘H(f)=t·e_K and the second is exactly c_K. Small cases checked: t a unit, R=0, constant Z with t=p (Z→Z_p→Z_p/Z), constant Z_p. The node is self-contained, statement-only and correctly cited, and it is not a restated clause. Duplicate search found no match. lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit and lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion give only local-RHom criteria for non-functorial limits, with no fiber triangle. lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison is for O_E coefficients only. lem-weil-pbc-torsion-limit-sheaf-completeness is for Noetherian constant rings only. Refs equal stmt_deps, uses and proof_deps; blueprint fields are present; there is no SGA. Accepted generic tools: lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus and lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem complete_heart_kernels (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}) (R : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R))] (a : (SheafOfModules.unit (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R)).sections) (_ha : Mono (globalSectionMultiplication R a)) (F : Model.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} R a) : (∀ (M N : ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R)) (g : M ⟶ N), IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F M → IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F N → IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F (kernel g) ∧ IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F (cokernel g) ∧ IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F (image g)) ∧ (∀ S : ShortComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R)), S.ShortExact → IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F S.X₁ → IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F S.X₃ → IsCompleteModule.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} F S.X₂)
lean.note: The existing universal PrincipalQuotientCompletion.Model specifies the quotient tower, K-flat computation, augmented Roos model and canonical unit. IsCompleteModule is precisely invertibility of that unit on the module in degree zero. Quantification over its canonical presentations makes no arbitrary choice of map or completion functor.
